about: The opening of the Fourth Branch, the branch of Math son of Mathonwy: to win Goewin for his brother Gilfaethwy, Gwydion tricks Pryderi of Dyfed out of his swine from Annwfn and so brings war on Gwynedd, which ends with Pryderi killed by Gwydion in single combat at Y Felenrhyd.

sentences.t: Math uab Mathonwy oed arglwyd ar Wyned, a Pryderi uab Pwyll oed arglwyd ar un cantref ar ugeint yn y Deheu.
sentences.l: Math son of Mathonwy was lord over Gwynedd, and Pryderi son of Pwyll was lord over one cantref on twenty in the South.
sentences.i: Math son of Mathonwy was lord over Gwynedd, and Pryderi son of Pwyll was lord over the one and twenty cantrefs of the South.
sentences.n: The Fourth Branch opens here; in Evans the M of Math is a large decorated initial. Math uab Mathonwy oed arglwyd: the subject comes first and the verb oed 'was' follows, the ordinary order of narrative (the abnormal sentence); before oed the particle a is not written, as often before a vowel. uab ← mab 'son', softened between two names. ar Wyned ← Gwyned, softened after ar 'over'. un cantref ar ugeint 'one cantref on twenty' is the Welsh way of counting twenty-one. y Deheu 'the South', that is south Wales; Pryderi is the son of Pwyll of the First Branch.

sentences.t: Sef oed y rei hynny, seith cantref Dyuet, a seith Morgannhwc, a phedwar Kyredigyawn, a thri Ystrat Tywi.
sentences.l: That-is, those were: seven cantrefs of-Dyfed, and seven of-Morgannwg, and four of-Ceredigion, and three of-Ystrad Tywi.
sentences.i: Those were the seven cantrefs of Dyfed, the seven of Morgannwg, the four of Ceredigion and the three of Ystrad Tywi.
sentences.n: Sef 'that is (it)' introduces the answer to an implied question — which were they? — and the sentence is built round it; English can drop it. y rei hynny 'those ones'. Morgannhwc is Morgannwg, so spelled here with -nhw-. a phedwar ← pedwar 'four' and a thri ← tri 'three': the spirant mutation after a 'and' (p > ph, t > th). Kyredigyawn is Ceredigion, with K for C and -yawn for -ion; later in the part (col. 86) Evans prints Keredigyawn, and both spellings are kept as he prints them. The sum is 7 + 7 + 4 + 3 = 21.

sentences.t: Ac yn yr oes honno Math uab Mathonwy ny bydei uyw, namyn tra uei y deudroet ymlyc croth morwyn, onyt kynwryf ryuel a'y llesteirei.
sentences.l: And in that age Math son of Mathonwy would-not-be alive, except while were his two-feet in-the-fold of-the-lap of-a-maiden, unless the tumult of-war it-was-that-prevented-him.
sentences.i: And in those days Math son of Mathonwy could not live unless his two feet lay in the lap of a maiden, save only when the tumult of war prevented him.
sentences.n: ny bydei 'would not be': bydei is the habitual imperfect of bot, 'used to be'; uyw ← byw 'alive', softened as the complement. tra uei 'while (they) were': uei ← bei, imperfect subjunctive of bot, softened after tra. y deudroet 'his two feet': deu 'two' softens troet > droet, written with one d. ymlyc 'in the fold of' is yn + plyc, with the nasal mutation (ym mhlyc) not fully shown by the spelling. croth is properly 'womb, belly'; here the lap. onyt 'unless'. a'y llesteirei 'that prevented him': a + the infixed object pronoun 'y 'him' + llesteirei, imperfect of llesteiraw 'hinder'.

sentences.t: Sef oed yn uorwyn gyt ac ef, Goewin uerch Pebin o Dol Pebin yn Aruon.
sentences.l: That-is, there-was as maiden with him, Goewin daughter of-Pebin from Dôl Pebin in Arfon.
sentences.i: The maiden with him was Goewin daughter of Pebin, from Dôl Pebin in Arfon.
sentences.n: Sef again: the sentence names who the maiden was. yn uorwyn 'as maiden': predicative yn, which softens morwyn > uorwyn (u = /v/). gyt ac ef 'with him' (gyt a 'together with'). uerch ← merch 'daughter', softened after a woman's name. Goewin is so spelled here and in col. 82; in col. 87 Evans prints Goewyn, and both are kept. Dol Pebin is Dôl Pebin; Aruon is Arfon, the cantref facing Anglesey.

sentences.t: A honno teccaf morwyn oed yn y hoes o'r a wydit yno.
sentences.l: And she, fairest maiden was in her age of those that were-known there.
sentences.i: And she was the fairest maiden of her time, of all that were known there.
sentences.n: honno 'that one (fem.)' stands first as the topic; then comes the predicate teccaf morwyn 'fairest maiden', and oed 'was' last. teccaf is the superlative of tec 'fair', and it comes before its noun. y hoes 'her age': oes 'age' takes h before its vowel after y 'her'. o'r a wydit 'of what was known': o'r 'of the', a the relative particle, wydit ← gwydit, the impersonal imperfect of gwybot 'know', softened after a. The ending -it is the old impersonal: 'one knew'.

sentences.t: Ac ynteu yg Kaer Dathyl yn Aruon yd oed y wastatrwyd.
sentences.l: And he-for-his-part, in Caer Dathyl in Arfon it-was that was his constant-dwelling.
sentences.i: And he had his settled seat at Caer Dathyl in Arfon.
sentences.n: ynteu 'he for his part', the conjunctive pronoun that sets a new subject against the last. The adverbial phrase is put first and yd (the particle before a vowel) leads to oed. yg Kaer: yn 'in' before K is written yg, the nasal mutation shown on the preposition but the K left plain. y wastatrwyd 'his constancy, his fixed residence' ← gwastatrwyd (gwastat 'constant, level'), softened after y 'his'. Caer Dathyl is in Arfon; its site is not certainly known.

sentences.t: Ac ny allei gylchu y wlat, namyn Giluathwy uab Don o a Euyd uab Don, o nyeint ueibon y chwaer, a'r teulu gyt ac wy y gylchu y wlat drostaw.
sentences.l: And he-could-not go-round the land, but Gilfaethwy son of Dôn o and Eueydd son of Dôn, as nephews sons of his sister, and the warband with them to go-round the land for-him.
sentences.i: And he could not go the circuit of the land himself; but Gilfaethwy son of Dôn and Eueydd son of Dôn, his nephews, his sister's sons, with the warband, went the circuit of the land for him.
sentences.n: ny allei 'he could not' ← gallei, imperfect of gallu, softened after ny. gylchu ← kylchu 'go round, make the circuit', softened as the verbal noun after the verb. y wlat ← gwlat 'land', softened after the feminine article. Two manuscript points. (1) The White Book names the second brother Euyd uab Don (Eueydd son of Dôn; the Red Book also has eueyd); later editions emend the name to Gwydion, who is the brother in the rest of the tale. (2) The o after the first uab Don is a stray letter, apparently the o of o nyeint begun too early; it is kept as written and means nothing. o nyeint, where the Red Book has y nyeint 'his nephews': the sense of o here ('as nephews', 'of the nephews') is uncertain. y chwaer 'his sister', that is Dôn, sister of Math. The last clause has no verb of its own (the second witness supplies one; the White Book does not): 'and the warband with them, to go round', the verb understood from gylchu. drostaw 'for him', dros conjugated (3 sg. masc.). teulu is the lord's warband (house: 'household-troop').

sentences.t: A'r uorwyn oed gyt a Math yn wastat; ac ynteu Giluaethwy uab Don a dodes y uryt ar y uorwyn, a'y charu hyt na wydat beth a wnay ymdanei.
sentences.l: And the maiden was with Math constantly; and he-for-his-part Gilfaethwy son of Dôn set his mind on the maiden, and her loving so-that he-did-not-know what he-should-do about-her.
sentences.i: The maiden was with Math always; and Gilfaethwy son of Dôn set his heart on her, and loved her until he did not know what to do for her.
sentences.n: y uorwyn ← morwyn, softened after the feminine article. yn wastat 'constantly' ← gwastat, softened after the adverbial yn. a dodes 'set, put', preterite of dodi. y uryt ← bryt 'mind, intent', softened after y 'his'. a'y charu 'and her loving': a 'and' + 'y 'her' + caru, which takes the spirant mutation after 'her' (c > ch). The verbal noun carries on the narrative where English wants 'and loved her'. Giluaethwy: so spelled here; Giluathwy just before. Both are in col. 82, as Evans prints them. wydat ← gwydat 'knew'. a wnay ← gwnaei 'would do', softened after a. ymdanei 'about her', ymdan conjugated (3 sg. fem.).

sentences.t: Ac nachaf y liw a'y wed a'y ansawd yn atueilaw o'y charyat, hyt nat oed hawd y adnabot.
sentences.l: And behold his colour and his face and his state wasting from his-loving-her, so-that it-was-not easy his knowing.
sentences.i: And see, his colour and his looks and his whole condition were wasting away for love of her, until it was hard to know him.
sentences.n: nachaf 'behold, lo', a narrative word for a sudden sight. y liw ← lliw 'colour', softened after y 'his'; wed ← gwed 'face, appearance' after 'y 'his'; ansawd 'state, condition'. atueilaw 'decay, waste' (modern adfeilio) with yn: 'wasting'. o'y charyat 'from love of her': o 'from' + 'y 'her' + caryat, spirant-mutated after 'her'. y adnabot 'his recognising', that is, to recognise him: y 'him' as the object of the verbal noun adnabot 'know, recognise'.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth Guydyon y urawd, synnyeit dydgweith arnaw yn graf.
sentences.l: That-is what Gwydion his brother did: gazing one-day on-him keenly.
sentences.i: One day Gwydion his brother looked at him closely.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth 'this is what (he) did', followed by the verbal noun that names the deed: synnyeit 'gazing, observing'. Guydyon is Gwydion, here spelled with gu for gw; Evans prints Guydyon, Gwydyon and the softened Wydyon at different places in the part, each kept as he prints it. y urawd ← brawd 'brother', softened after y 'his'. dydgweith 'one day'. arnaw 'on him', ar conjugated (3 sg. masc.). yn graf ← craf 'keen, close', softened after the adverbial yn.

sentences.t: “A was,” heb ef, “pa deryw ytti?”
sentences.l: “Lad,” said he, “what has-befallen to-you?”
sentences.i: “Lad,” he said, “what has come over you?”
sentences.n: A was 'lad': the vocative particle a softens gwas 'youth, lad' > was. pa deryw 'what has happened': deryw is the perfect of daruot 'happen, befall'; in Evans the y of deryw is written above the r and is brought into the line (the second witness's derw is wrong). ytti 'to you', the preposition y conjugated (2 sg.), with doubled tt; when Gwydion repeats the question a little later it is spelled yti.

sentences.t: “Pa ham?” heb ynteu.
sentences.l: “Why?” said he-for-his-part.
sentences.i: “Why?” said he.
sentences.n: Pa ham 'why' (modern paham). heb ynteu 'said he for his part', the usual tag when the other speaker answers.

sentences.t: “Beth a wely di arnaf i?”
sentences.l: “What do-you-see you on-me I?”
sentences.i: “What do you see in me?”
sentences.n: Beth 'what' ← peth 'thing', the softened form used as the question word. a wely ← gwely, 2 sg. present of gwelet 'see', softened after a; di is the affixed pronoun 'you'. arnaf i 'on me', ar conjugated (1 sg.) with i repeating 'me'. The speech runs on from the last unit without a new tag.

sentences.t: “Gwelaf arnat,” heb ef, “colli dy bryt a'th liw, a pha deryw yti?”
sentences.l: “I-see on-you,” said he, “losing your looks and your colour; and what has-befallen to-you?”
sentences.i: “I see in you,” he said, “the loss of your looks and your colour; and what has come over you?”
sentences.n: Gwelaf 'I see', 1 sg. present of gwelet. arnat 'on you', ar conjugated (2 sg.). colli 'losing', a verbal noun used as the object of 'see'. dy bryt ← pryt 'form, looks', softened after dy 'your'. a'th liw 'and your colour': a + 'th 'your', which softens lliw > liw. yti, the same 'to you' spelled ytti two units back.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd urawt,” heb ef, “yr hynn a deryw ymi ny frwytha ymi y adef y neb.”
sentences.l: “Lord brother,” said he, “that which has-befallen to-me, it-will-not-profit to-me its confessing to anyone.”
sentences.i: “Lord brother,” he said, “what has befallen me, it will do me no good to tell anyone.”
sentences.n: Arglwyd urawt 'lord brother': urawt ← brawt, softened in address after the title. yr hynn a 'that which'. ymi 'to me', y conjugated (1 sg.). ny frwytha 'will not bear fruit, will not avail' ← ffrwythaw; the manuscript writes f for /f/ here. y adef 'its confessing', to confess it: y 'it' + adef 'acknowledge, admit' (modern addef). y neb 'to anyone'.

sentences.t: “Beth yw hynny, eneit?” heb ef.
sentences.l: “What is that, soul?” said he.
sentences.i: “What is it, my soul?” he said.
sentences.n: Beth yw hynny 'what is that'. eneit 'soul' is a term of endearment between kinsmen, 'my dear'. heb ef 'said he': Gwydion is speaking.

sentences.t: “Ti a wdost,” heb ynteu, “kynedyf Math uab Mathonwy; ba hustyng bynnac, yr y uychanet, o'r a uo y rwng dynnyon, o ry kyuarfo y guynt ac ef, ef a'y guybyd.”
sentences.l: “You it-is-that know,” said he-for-his-part, “the-peculiar-gift of-Math son of Mathonwy: whatever whisper, for its smallness, of what may-be between men, if the wind has-met with it, he it-is-that will-know-it.”
sentences.i: “You know,” he said, “the gift that belongs to Math son of Mathonwy: any whisper whatever between men, however low, once the wind has met it, he will know of it.”
sentences.n: Ti a wdost 'you know': subject first, then a, then wdost ← gwdost, 2 sg. present of gwybot, softened after a. kynedyf 'peculiar nature, innate gift'. ba hustyng bynnac 'whatever whisper': ba … bynnac 'whatever'. yr y uychanet 'however small (it be)': yr 'for' + y 'its' + bychanet, the equative of bychan 'small', softened after y; the construction yr + possessive + equative is concessive. o'r a uo 'of what may be': uo ← bo, present subjunctive of bot. y rwng 'between'. o ry kyuarfo 'if (the wind) has met': o 'if', the perfective particle ry, and kyuarfo, present subjunctive of kyuaruot 'meet'; ry usually softens, but the k is written plain. ef a'y guybyd 'he will know it': 'y is the infixed object 'it', and guybyd (gwybyd), 3 sg. present-future of gwybot, stays unsoftened after it.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb y Guydyon, “taw di bellach.
sentences.l: “Yes,” said Gwydion, “be-silent you now.
sentences.i: “Yes,” said Gwydion, “say no more.
sentences.n: heb y Guydyon 'said Gwydion': heb y before a name, heb ef before a pronoun. taw 'be silent', the imperative of tewi; di repeats 'you'. bellach 'now, from now on, any further'. The speech continues in the next unit.

sentences.t: Mi a wnn dy uedwl di; caru Goewin yd wyt ti.”
sentences.l: I it-is-that know your thought: loving Goewin are you.”
sentences.i: I know your thought: it is Goewin you love.”
sentences.n: Mi a wnn 'I know': wnn ← gwnn, 1 sg. present of gwybot, softened after a. dy uedwl ← medwl 'thought', softened after dy. caru Goewin yd wyt ti 'loving Goewin you are': the verbal-noun phrase is put first for emphasis and linked to the verb by yd; this fronting does stress, which is why English needs 'it is Goewin'.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth ynteu yna, pan wybu ef adnabot o'y urawt y uedwl, dodi ucheneit dromhaf yn y byt.
sentences.l: That-is what he-for-his-part did then, when he knew the-recognising by his brother of his thought: putting the heaviest sigh in the world.
sentences.i: Then, when he knew that his brother had read his thought, he heaved the heaviest sigh in the world.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth … dodi 'what he did … was putting (a sigh)'. wybu ← gwybu, preterite of gwybot, softened after pan 'when'. adnabot o'y urawt y uedwl 'knowing by his brother his thought': a verbal noun with its doer given by o 'by' (o'y = o + y 'his'), and its object y uedwl; urawt ← brawt and uedwl ← medwl, both softened after y 'his'. ucheneit 'sigh' is feminine, so the adjective after it softens: dromhaf ← tromhaf, the superlative of trwm 'heavy'.

sentences.t: “Taw, eneit, a'th ucheneidaw,” heb ef, “nyt o hynny y goruydir.
sentences.l: “Be-silent, soul, with your sighing,” said he, “not from that it-is-prevailed.
sentences.i: “Hush, my soul, and leave your sighing,” he said, “it is not by that the day is won.
sentences.n: Taw 'be silent' again. a'th ucheneidaw 'with your sighing': a 'with' + 'th 'your'; ucheneidaw is the verbal noun of ucheneit. nyt o hynny 'not from that': the negative nyt goes before a fronted phrase. y goruydir 'it is overcome, one prevails': goruydir is the impersonal present (ending -ir) of goruot 'overcome, win'.

sentences.t: Minheu a baraf,” heb ef, “cany ellir heb hynny, dygyuori Gwyned a Phowys a Deheubarth y geissaw y uorwyn; a byd lawen di, a mi a'y paraf yt.”
sentences.l: I-for-my-part it-is-that will-cause,” said he, “since it-cannot-be-done without that, the-raising of-Gwynedd and Powys and Deheubarth to seek the maiden; and be you glad, and I it-is-that will-cause-it for-you.”
sentences.i: I will bring about,” he said, “since it cannot be done without it, the mustering of Gwynedd and Powys and Deheubarth in quest of the maiden; so be glad, and I will bring it about for you.”
sentences.n: Minheu 'I for my part'. a baraf ← paraf 'I will cause', 1 sg. present-future of peri, softened after a. cany ellir 'since it cannot be done': cany 'since not', and ellir ← gellir, the impersonal present of gallu, softened. dygyuori 'raise (a host), muster', with Gwyned, Powys (a Phowys, spirant after a) and Deheubarth as its objects. A war will take Math out of the maiden's lap: that is the plan. y geissaw ← keissaw 'seek', softened after y 'to'. byd lawen 'be glad': byd is the 2 sg. imperative of bot, and llawen softens after it. a'y paraf 'I will cause it': the infixed 'y 'it' again with no mutation after it. yt 'to you'.

sentences.t: Ac ar hynny at Uath uab Mathonwy yd aethant wy.
sentences.l: And on that, to Math son of Mathonwy it-was that they-went they.
sentences.i: And upon that they went to Math son of Mathonwy.
sentences.n: ar hynny 'on that, thereupon'. at Uath ← Math, softened after at 'to'. The adverbial phrase is put first and yd leads to the verb aethant 'they went' (preterite of mynet); wy repeats 'they'.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb y Guydyon, “mi a gigleu dyuot y'r Deheu y ryw bryuet ni doeth y'r ynys honn eiroet.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said Gwydion, “I it-is-that heard the coming to the South of the kind of beasts that came-not to this island ever.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” said Gwydion, “I have heard that there have come into the South a kind of beasts that never came to this island before.”
sentences.n: Arglwyd 'Lord' in address. a gigleu ← kigleu 'I heard', an old 1 sg. preterite of clywet, softened after a. dyuot 'the coming', a verbal noun that stands as the object, 'that … had come'. y'r 'to the'. y ryw bryuet 'the kind of creatures': ryw softens what follows, pryuet > bryuet. pryuet (plural of pryf) is 'creatures, beasts' of any kind, not only insects. ni doeth 'did not come'; the soft mutation of d (dd) is not shown in this spelling. y'r ynys honn 'this island', Britain. eiroet 'ever'.

sentences.t: “Pwy eu henw wy?” heb ef.
sentences.l: “What their name they?” said he.
sentences.i: “What are they called?” he said.
sentences.n: Pwy 'who' is the question word used for asking a name. eu henw 'their name': henw ← enw takes h after eu 'their'. wy repeats 'they'.

sentences.t: “Hobeu, Arglwyd.”
sentences.l: “Hobeu, Lord.”
sentences.i: “Hobeu, Lord.”
sentences.n: Hobeu is the plural of hob, an old word for a pig; the beasts are named by it here, and the narrator's aside two units on turns on it. It is kept untranslated in English for that reason. Evans has a dot after arglwyd here: it is punctuation, and the speech ends there.

sentences.t: “Pa ryw aniueileit yw y rei hynny?”
sentences.l: “What kind-of animals are those?”
sentences.i: “What sort of animals are those?”
sentences.n: Pa ryw 'what kind of'. aniueileit 'animals', plural of aniueil. y rei hynny 'those ones'. Math is asking; the speeches now run without tags.

sentences.t: “Aniueileit bychein, guell eu kic no chic eidon.
sentences.l: “Animals small, better their flesh than the-flesh of-oxen.
sentences.i: “Small animals, whose flesh is better than the flesh of oxen.
sentences.n: bychein 'small', the plural form of the adjective bychan, agreeing with aniueileit. guell 'better', the comparative of da, with gu for gw. no chic 'than the flesh': no 'than' brings the spirant mutation, kic > chic. eidon 'ox, bullock'.

sentences.t: Bychein ynt wynteu; ac y maent yn symudaw enweu.
sentences.l: Small are they-for-their-part; and they-are changing names.
sentences.i: They are small; and they are changing their name.
sentences.n: Bychein ynt wynteu 'small are they': the predicate first, then ynt 'are' and wynteu 'they for their part'. y maent yn symudaw 'they are changing': y the particle before maent, and yn with the verbal noun for the continuous. enweu 'names', plural of enw. The meaning is given in the next unit: the beasts are now called by another name.

sentences.t: Moch y gelwir weithon.”
sentences.l: Pigs it-is they-are-called now.”
sentences.i: Swine is what they are called now.”
sentences.n: Moch 'pigs, swine' is put first, and the verb follows with the particle y. y gelwir 'they are called': gelwir is the impersonal present of galw 'call', 'one calls (them)'. weithon 'now, by now'. The old name hob is giving way to moch, the word that will name the places of the coming journey (Mochdref, Mochnant).

sentences.t: “Pwy biewynt wy?”
sentences.l: “Who owns they?”
sentences.i: “Whose are they?”
sentences.n: biewynt is a 3 pl. form of the verb bieu 'own, belong to', agreeing with wy 'they': 'whose are they?'. The verb bieu is the ancestor of modern piau.

sentences.t: “Pryderi uab Pwyll, yd anuonet idaw o Annwn y gan Arawn Urenhin Annwn.”
sentences.l: “Pryderi son of Pwyll; they-were-sent to-him from Annwfn from Arawn King of-Annwfn.”
sentences.i: “Pryderi son of Pwyll; they were sent to him from Annwfn by Arawn, King of Annwfn.”
sentences.n: yd anuonet 'they were sent': anuonet is the impersonal preterite (ending -et) of anuon 'send'. idaw 'to him', y conjugated (3 sg. masc.). y gan 'from (the hand of)'. Urenhin ← brenhin 'king', softened after the name. Annwn is Annwfn, here spelled without its middle consonant; later in the part Evans has Annwuyn. Arawn, King of Annwfn, is the king whose kingdom Pwyll held for a year in the First Branch.

sentences.t: (Ac etwa yd ys yn cadw o'r enw hwnnw hanner hwch, hanner hob.)
sentences.l: (And still one-is keeping of that name: half a-sow, half a-hob.)
sentences.i: (And something of that name is kept to this day, in the saying hanner hwch, hanner hob, ‘half sow, half hob’.)
sentences.n: A narrator's aside, set in brackets as in the second witness. etwa 'still, yet'. yd ys 'one is': ys is the impersonal present of bot. yn cadw 'keeping'. o'r enw hwnnw 'of that name', some trace of it. hanner hwch, hanner hob: hwch is 'sow, pig'; what the saying meant (a side or half carcass of pork has been suggested) is uncertain.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “ba furuf y keffir wy y gantaw ef?”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “what way are-they-got they from-him he?”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “and how are they to be had from him?”
sentences.n: Ie 'Yes'. Evans prints a mark like ! after heb at the line end; it is not a letter and nothing is missing. ba furuf 'what way': ba 'what' softens ffuruf 'form, manner' (written with one f, as f = /f/). y keffir 'they are got': keffir is the impersonal present of kaffael 'get'. y gantaw ef 'from him': y gan 'from', gan conjugated (3 sg. masc.) with ef repeating 'him'.

sentences.t: “Mi a af ar uyn deudecuet, yn rith beird, Arglwyd, y erchi y moch.”
sentences.l: “I it-is-that will-go as my twelfth, in the-guise of-poets, Lord, to ask-for the pigs.”
sentences.i: “I will go with eleven others, in the guise of poets, Lord, to ask for the swine.”
sentences.n: Mi a af 'I will go', 1 sg. present of mynet. ar uyn deudecuet 'on my twelfth': the idiom means 'myself and eleven others', a band of twelve. uyn 'my' is a form of uy. yn rith 'in the shape, the guise of'; beird 'poets', plural of bard (final d = /ð/). y erchi 'to ask for'.

sentences.t: “Ef a ry eill ych necau,” heb ynteu.
sentences.l: “He it-is-that may refuse you,” said he-for-his-part.
sentences.i: “He may refuse you,” he said.
sentences.n: Ef a ry eill 'he may be able': eill ← geill, 3 sg. present of gallu, softened after a; the particle ry here gives the sense of possibility. ych necau 'your refusing', to refuse you: ych 'you' as the object of the verbal noun necau 'refuse' (modern nacáu).

sentences.t: “Nit drwc uyn trawscwyd i, Arglwyd,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “Not bad my contrivance I, Lord,” said he.
sentences.i: “My plan is not a bad one, Lord,” he said.
sentences.n: Nit drwc 'not bad': nit 'not' goes before the fronted predicate. uyn trawscwyd i 'my contrivance': trawscwyd 'device, expedient, stratagem' is a rare word; it comes again in Gwydion's men's question a little later. Evans prints a \ mark after drwc; it is not a letter and nothing is missing.

sentences.t: “Ny doaf i heb y moch.”
sentences.l: “I-will-not-come I without the pigs.”
sentences.i: “I will not come back without the swine.”
sentences.n: Ny doaf i 'I will not come': doaf is 1 sg. present-future of dyuot. Gwydion's speech runs on; no new tag.

sentences.t: “En llawen,” heb ynteu, “kerda ragot.”
sentences.l: “Gladly,” said he-for-his-part, “go before-you.”
sentences.i: “Gladly,” he said. “Go on your way.”
sentences.n: En llawen 'gladly': en is yn, the adverbial particle, and llawen keeps its ll after it. kerda 'go, walk', imperative of kerdet. ragot ← racot 'before you', rac conjugated (2 sg.), softened after the verb: 'go forth'.

sentences.t: Ef a aeth, a Giluathwy, a deguyr gyt ac wynt, hyt yg Heredigyawn, yn y lle a elwir Rudlan Teiui yr awrhon; yd oed llys yno y Pryderi; ac yn rith beird y doethant ymywn.
sentences.l: He it-is-that went, and Gilfaethwy, and ten-men with them, as-far-as to Ceredigion, to the place that is-called Rhuddlan Teifi this hour; there-was a-court there to Pryderi; and in the-guise of-poets it-was that they-came in.
sentences.i: He went, with Gilfaethwy and ten men besides, into Ceredigion, to the place now called Rhuddlan Teifi; Pryderi had a court there; and in the guise of poets they came in.
sentences.n: Ef a aeth 'he went'. deguyr 'ten men': deg + gwyr, softened in the compound. hyt yg Heredigyawn 'as far as Ceredigion': yn 'in' + Keredigyawn with the nasal mutation; Evans writes it gh (ygheredigyawn), as he writes yghymherued later; the word is divided yg Heredigyawn here, like yg Kaer. a elwir 'that is called' ← gelwir, impersonal present of galw, softened after a. yr awrhon 'now'. llys y Pryderi 'a court to Pryderi', a court of Pryderi's. Rhuddlan Teifi was on the Teifi. ymywn 'in, inside'.

sentences.t: Llawen uuant wrthunt.
sentences.l: Glad they-were towards-them.
sentences.i: They were made welcome.
sentences.n: Llawen 'glad' is put first and the verb follows: uuant ← buant 'they were', preterite of bot, softened. wrthunt 'towards them', wrth conjugated (3 pl.): Pryderi's people were glad of them.

sentences.t: Ar neillaw Pryderi y gossodet Guydyon y nos honno.
sentences.l: At the-one-side of-Pryderi it-was Gwydion was-placed that night.
sentences.i: That night Gwydion was seated at Pryderi's side.
sentences.n: Ar neillaw 'at the side of'. y gossodet 'was placed': gossodet is the impersonal preterite of gossot 'place, set'. Seating beside the lord was a mark of honour.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb y Pryderi, “da yw genhym ni cahel kyuarwydyt gan rei o'r gwreinc racco.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said Pryderi, “good is with us getting a-tale from some of the young-men yonder.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” said Pryderi, “we should be glad to have a tale from some of the young men yonder.”
sentences.n: da yw genhym ni 'it is good with us', we should like: genhym 'with us', gan conjugated (1 pl.). cahel 'getting', a spelling of kael (kaffael). kyuarwydyt 'tale, story-lore'. gwreinc 'young men', plural of gwreang 'youth'. racco 'yonder'.

sentences.t: “Moes yw genhym ni, Arglwyd,” heb y Guydyon, “y nos gyntaf y delher at wr mawr, dywedut o'r penkerd.
sentences.l: “Custom is with us, Lord,” said Gwydion, “the first night that one-comes to a-great man, speaking by the chief-poet.
sentences.i: “It is our custom, Lord,” said Gwydion, “that on the first night one comes to a great man, the chief poet speaks.
sentences.n: Moes 'custom'. y delher 'one comes': delher is the impersonal present subjunctive of dyuot. at wr mawr 'to a great man': wr ← gwr, softened after at. dywedut o'r penkerd 'speaking by the chief poet': a verbal noun with its doer given by o, as earlier with adnabot. penkerd 'chief of song', the head poet of a company.

sentences.t: Mi a dywedaf gyuarwydyd yn llawen.”
sentences.l: I it-is-that will-tell a-tale gladly.”
sentences.i: I will tell a tale gladly.”
sentences.n: Mi a dywedaf 'I will tell'. gyuarwydyd ← kyuarwydyd, softened as the object after the verb; the same word as kyuarwydyt with -d for -t. yn llawen 'gladly', with the adverbial yn.

sentences.t: Ynteu Wydyon goreu kyuarwyd yn y byt oed.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part Gwydion, the best storyteller in the world he-was.
sentences.i: Gwydion was the best storyteller in the world.
sentences.n: Ynteu Wydyon 'he, Gwydion': the name is softened, as Evans prints it here (Wydyon). goreu kyuarwyd 'best storyteller': goreu 'best' stands before its noun. kyuarwyd 'one who knows the ways, guide; storyteller'. The predicate is put first and oed comes at the end.

sentences.t: A'r nos honno, didanu y llys a wnaeth ar ymdidaneu digrif a chyuarwydyt, yny oed hoff gan paub o'r llys, ac yn didan gan Pryderi ymdidan ac ef.
sentences.l: And that night, entertaining the court he-did with talk pleasant and tales, so-that he-was beloved by everyone of the court, and pleasant by Pryderi conversing with him.
sentences.i: And that night he entertained the court with pleasant talk and tales, until everyone in the court loved him, and Pryderi found it a delight to talk with him.
sentences.n: didanu y llys a wnaeth 'entertaining the court he did': a verbal noun and its object, then a wnaeth 'he did', which makes it finite, 'he entertained'. ar ymdidaneu digrif 'with pleasant talk': ymdidaneu, plural of ymdidan 'conversation'. a chyuarwydyt ← kyuarwydyt, spirant after a. yny 'until, so that'. hoff 'dear, beloved'. paub 'everyone', the manuscript spelling of pawb. yn didan gan Pryderi 'pleasant with Pryderi': a pleasure to him.

sentences.t: Ac ar diwed hynny, “Arglwyd,” heb ef, “ae guell y gwna neb uy neges i wrthyt ti no mi uu hun?”
sentences.l: And at the-end of-that, “Lord,” said he, “is better that anyone does my errand I with-you you than I my self?”
sentences.i: And at the end of it, “Lord,” he said, “would anyone do my errand with you better than I myself?”
sentences.n: ae 'is it?', the question particle before a fronted predicate. guell 'better'. y gwna 'that (anyone) does': gwna, 3 sg. present of gwneuthur. uy neges i 'my errand'. wrthyt ti 'with you', wrth conjugated (2 sg.). no 'than'. mi uu hun 'I myself': uu hun, apparently for uy hun 'my self'.

sentences.t: “Na well,” heb ynteu.
sentences.l: “No better,” said he-for-his-part.
sentences.i: “No,” he said.
sentences.n: Na well 'not better': na 'no, not' in an answer softens gwell > well. The answer repeats the verb or word of the question, here guell.

sentences.t: “Tauawt lawn da yw y teu di.”
sentences.l: “A-tongue full good is yours.”
sentences.i: “Yours is a very good tongue.”
sentences.n: Tauawt 'tongue' (modern tafod; u = /v/). lawn ← llawn 'full', softened before the adjective it strengthens: 'full good', very good. y teu 'yours', the independent possessive (2 sg.). The speech continues without a tag; Pryderi is speaking.

sentences.t: “Llyna uy neges inheu, Arglwyd, ymadolwyn a thidi am yr aniueileit a anuonet it o Annwuyn.”
sentences.l: “There-is my errand I-for-my-part, Lord: beseeching with you-yourself for the animals that were-sent to-you from Annwfn.”
sentences.i: “Then this is my errand, Lord: to beg of you the animals that were sent to you from Annwfn.”
sentences.n: Llyna 'there is, that is'. ymadolwyn a 'beseech, entreat': a thidi 'with you yourself', the reduplicated pronoun tidi, with spirant mutation after a. a anuonet 'that were sent', impersonal preterite again. it 'to you'. Annwuyn is the usual spelling of Annwfn (u = /v/); compare Annwn above.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “hawssaf yn y byt oed hynny by na bei ammot y rof a'm gwlat amdanunt; sef yw hynny, nat elont y genhyf yny hilyont eu deu kymeint yn y wlat.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “easiest in the world would-be that, were-it not that-there-were a-covenant between me and my land about-them; that-is, that they-should-not-go from-me until they-breed their twice as-much in the land.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “nothing in the world would be easier, were it not for a covenant between me and my land concerning them: that they shall not go from me until they have bred twice their number in the land.”
sentences.n: hawssaf 'easiest', superlative of hawd. oed here is 'would be'. by na bei 'if it were not that': by is a spelling of pei 'if', and bei the imperfect subjunctive of bot. ammot 'covenant, agreement'. y rof a'm gwlat 'between me and my land', as in the oath y rof a Duw; a'm is a 'and' + 'm 'my'. amdanunt 'about them', am conjugated (3 pl.). sef yw hynny 'that is'. nat elont 'that they should not go': elont is the 3 pl. present subjunctive of mynet. y genhyf 'from me'. yny hilyont 'until they breed': hilyont, 3 pl. present subjunctive of hilyaw. eu deu kymeint 'their two-as-much', double their number.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb ynteu, “minheu a allaf dy rydhau ditheu o'r geireu hynny.
sentences.l: “Lord,” said he-for-his-part, “I-for-my-part it-is-that can free you you-for-your-part from those words.
sentences.i: “Lord,” he said, “I can free you from those words.
sentences.n: Minheu a allaf 'I can'. dy rydhau 'your freeing', to free you: dy 'you' as the object of the verbal noun rydhau 'set free' (modern rhyddhau; r is written for rh, so no mutation shows). ditheu ← titheu 'you for your part', softened. o'r geireu hynny 'from those words': geireu 'words', plural of geir.

sentences.t: Sef ual y gallaf, na dyro im y moch heno, ac nacaha ui ohonunt.
sentences.l: That-is how I-can: do-not-give to-me the pigs tonight, and refuse me of-them.
sentences.i: This is how I can do it: do not give me the swine tonight — and do not refuse me them either.
sentences.n: Sef ual y gallaf 'this is how I can'. na dyro 'do not give': na with the imperative of rodi. im 'to me'. heno 'tonight'. ac nacaha ui ohonunt: as written, 'and refuse me of them' — the White Book has no negative here. The sense intended is 'and do not refuse me them', as the Red Book has it (ac na naccaa ui); a na has probably dropped out before nacaha (both begin na-). Nothing is supplied, since the White Book shows no gap. nacaha is the imperative of nacau 'refuse'; ui ← mi 'me', softened as the object; ohonunt 'of them', o conjugated (3 pl.).

sentences.t: Auory minheu a dangossaf gyfnewit amdanunt wy.”
sentences.l: Tomorrow I-for-my-part it-is-that will-show an-exchange for-them they.”
sentences.i: Tomorrow I will show you what I can give in exchange for them.”
sentences.n: Auory 'tomorrow' (u = /v/). a dangossaf 'I will show', 1 sg. present-future of dangos. gyfnewit ← kyfnewit 'exchange', softened as the object. amdanunt wy 'for them'.

sentences.t: A'r nos honno yd aethont ef a'y gedymdeithon y'r lletty ar y kynghor.
sentences.l: And that night it-was they-went he and his companions to the lodging, to the counsel.
sentences.i: And that night he and his companions went to their lodging to take counsel.
sentences.n: yd aethont 'they went', a variant of aethant. a'y gedymdeithon 'and his companions': gedymdeithon ← kedymdeithon, softened after 'y 'his'. y'r lletty 'to the lodging'. ar y kynghor 'on the counsel', to deliberate.

sentences.t: “A wyr,” heb ef, “ny chawni y moch oc eu herchi.”
sentences.l: “Men,” said he, “we-will-not-get the pigs from their asking.”
sentences.i: “Men,” he said, “we shall not get the swine by asking for them.”
sentences.n: A wyr 'O men': the vocative particle softens gwyr > wyr. ny chawni 'we will not get': cawn, 1 pl. present of kaffael, with the spirant after ny (c > ch) and ni 'we' written onto it. oc eu herchi 'from their asking', by asking for them: oc is the form of o 'from' before eu 'their', and erchi takes h after eu.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb wynte, “pa drawscwyd y keir wynteu?”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said they, “what contrivance they-are-got they?”
sentences.i: “Yes,” they said, “and by what device are they to be had?”
sentences.n: heb wynte 'said they': wynte is a spelling of wynteu 'they for their part'. pa drawscwyd 'what contrivance': pa softens trawscwyd > drawscwyd. y keir 'they are got', the impersonal present of kaffael (keffir earlier in the part is the same tense).

sentences.t: “Mi a baraf eu cael,” heb y Guydyon.
sentences.l: “I it-is-that will-cause their getting,” said Gwydion.
sentences.i: “I will see that they are got,” said Gwydion.
sentences.n: Mi a baraf 'I will cause', as in his promise to Gilfaethwy. eu cael 'their getting': eu 'their' + cael (kael), the object of the verbal noun.

sentences.t: Ac yna yd aeth ef yn y geluydodeu, ac y dechreuawt dangos y hut, ac yd hudwys deudec emys, a deudec milgi bronwyn du pob un o honunt, a deudec torch, a deudec kynllyuan arnunt, a neb o'r a guelei, ni wydat na bydynt eur;
sentences.l: And then it-was he-went into his arts, and he-began showing his magic, and he-conjured twelve stallions, and twelve greyhounds, white-breasted black each one of-them, and twelve collars, and twelve leashes on-them, and anyone of those-who saw, he-did-not-know that they-were-not gold;
sentences.i: Then he went about his arts and began to work his magic, and he conjured up twelve stallions, and twelve greyhounds, each of them black with a white breast, and twelve collars and twelve leashes on them, such that no one who saw them could have told they were not gold;
sentences.n: yn y geluydodeu 'into his arts': keluydodeu, plural of keluydyt 'craft, art', softened after y 'his'. y dechreuawt 'he began': -awt is an old ending of the 3 sg. preterite (modern -odd). hut 'magic, enchantment'. yd hudwys 'he conjured', preterite in -wys of hudaw 'enchant'. emys 'stallions', plural of amws. milgi 'greyhound'; bronwyn 'white-breasted'. torch 'collar, torque'. kynllyuan 'leash': Evans prints kynllyuan without the i of the second witness's kynillyuan, as the plural kynllyuaneu later. a neb o'r a guelei 'and anyone of those who saw': guelei, imperfect of gwelet, with gu for gw and left unsoftened after a, as written (the second witness's added e is not in the White Book and is not needed). ni wydat na bydynt eur 'did not know that they were not gold': bydynt, imperfect of bot (3 pl.).

sentences.t: a deudec kyfrwy ar y meirch, ac am pob lle y dylyei hayarn uot arnunt, y bydei gwbyl o eur; a'r frwyneu yn un weith a hynny.
sentences.l: and twelve saddles on the horses, and about every place that iron ought to-be on-them, there-was wholly of gold; and the bridles in one work with that.
sentences.i: and twelve saddles on the horses, and wherever there should have been iron on them, it was all of gold; and the bridles were of a piece with them.
sentences.n: The sentence runs on from the last; it is cut at the semicolon for length. kyfrwy 'saddle'. y dylyei 'that (iron) ought': dylyei, imperfect of dylyu 'ought, be due'. hayarn 'iron'. uot ← bot 'to be', softened after its subject. y bydei 'there would be, there was'. gwbyl o eur 'wholly of gold'. a'r frwyneu 'and the bridles' (ffrwyneu, written with one f). yn un weith a hynny 'in one work with that', made all of a piece.

sentences.t: A'r meirch ac a'r cwn y doeth ef at Pryderi.
sentences.l: With the horses and with the dogs it-was he-came to Pryderi.
sentences.i: He came to Pryderi with the horses and the hounds.
sentences.n: A'r meirch ac a'r cwn 'with the horses and with the dogs': a 'with' (a'r 'with the'), and ac 'and' before the second. meirch 'horses', plural of march. The phrase is put first, and y leads to the verb doeth 'came'.

sentences.t: “Dyd da it, Arglwyd,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “Day good to-you, Lord,” said he.
sentences.i: “Good day to you, Lord,” he said.
sentences.n: Dyd da 'good day', the greeting. it 'to you', the preposition i/y conjugated (2 sg.).

sentences.t: “Duw a ro da it,” heb ef, “a graessaw wrthyt.”
sentences.l: “God may-he-give good to-you,” said he, “and welcome towards-you.”
sentences.i: “God give you good,” he said, “and welcome to you.”
sentences.n: Duw a ro 'God give': ro is the 3 sg. present subjunctive of rodi, used for a wish (rodo in other parts). graessaw 'welcome', with wrthyt 'towards you', wrth conjugated (2 sg.). The greeting and its answer are the set pair.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb ef, “llyma rydit yti am y geir a dywedeist neithwyr am y moch, nas rodut ac nas guerthut.
sentences.l: “Lord,” said he, “here-is freedom for-you from the word that you-said last-night about the pigs: that-you-would-not-give-them and that-you-would-not-sell-them.
sentences.i: “Lord,” he said, “here is your release from the word you spoke last night about the swine, that you would neither give them nor sell them.
sentences.n: llyma 'here is'. rydit 'freedom, release' (modern rhyddid; r for rh). yti 'to you'. am y geir 'about the word': geir 'word, pledge'. a dywedeist 'that you said', 2 sg. preterite of dywedut. neithwyr 'last night'. nas rodut ac nas guerthut 'that you would not give them and would not sell them': nas is the negative with the infixed object 's 'them'; rodut and guerthut are 2 sg. imperfect, used as conditional, of rodi 'give' and guerthu 'sell'.

sentences.t: Titheu a elly gyfnewit yr a uo guell.
sentences.l: You-for-your-part it-is-that can exchange for what may-be better.
sentences.i: You may exchange them for something better.
sentences.n: Titheu 'you for your part'. a elly ← gelly 'you can', 2 sg. present of gallu, softened after a. gyfnewit ← kyfnewit 'exchange', softened after the verb. yr a uo guell 'for what may be better': yr 'for', uo ← bo, present subjunctive of bot.

sentences.t: Minheu a rodaf y deudeg meirch hynn ual y maent yn gyueir, ac eu kyfrwyeu, ac eu frwyneu, a'r deudec milgi ac eu torcheu ac eu kynllyuaneu, ual y guely, a'r deudec taryan eureit a wely di racco.”
sentences.l: I-for-my-part it-is-that will-give these twelve horses as they-are, in-harness, and their saddles, and their bridles, and the twelve greyhounds and their collars and their leashes, as you-see, and the twelve shields gilded that you-see you yonder.”
sentences.i: I will give these twelve horses, harnessed as they are, with their saddles and their bridles, and the twelve greyhounds with their collars and leashes, as you see them, and the twelve gilded shields you see over there.”
sentences.n: Minheu a rodaf 'I will give'. deudeg meirch: a numeral normally takes the singular noun, but here it takes the plural meirch. yn gyueir 'equipped, in harness' ← kyueir, softened after yn. ac eu 'and their' (the sense is 'with their'). kynllyuaneu 'leashes', plural of kynllyuan. ual y guely 'as you see': guely, 2 sg. present of gwelet. taryan eureit 'gilded shield(s)'. a wely di racco 'that you see yonder'.

sentences.t: (Y rei hynny a rithassei ef o'r madalch).
sentences.l: (Those it-was-that he-had-conjured from the fungus).
sentences.i: (These he had fashioned by magic out of toadstools.)
sentences.n: Another narrator's aside in brackets. rithassei 'he had shaped by magic', the pluperfect (ending -assei) of rithaw, from rith 'shape, guise'. madalch 'fungi, toadstools'. The shields, and by implication the rest, will not last.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “ni a gymerwn gynghor.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “we it-is-that will-take counsel.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “we will take counsel.”
sentences.n: ni a gymerwn 'we will take': gymerwn ← kymerwn, 1 pl. present of kymryt, softened after a. gynghor ← kynghor 'counsel', softened as the object.

sentences.t: Sef a gaussant yn y kynghor, rodi y moch e Wydyon, a chymryt y meirch a'r cwn a'r taryaneu y gantaw ynteu.
sentences.l: That-is what they-got in the counsel: giving the pigs to Gwydion, and taking the horses and the dogs and the shields from-him he-for-his-part.
sentences.i: And the counsel they came to was to give the swine to Gwydion and to take the horses and the hounds and the shields from him.
sentences.n: Sef a gaussant 'what they got': gaussant ← kawssant, 3 pl. preterite of kaffael, softened after a. The decision is given in verbal nouns: rodi 'giving', a chymryt 'and taking' (spirant after a). e Wydyon 'to Gwydion': e is a spelling of y 'to', which softens Gwydyon. y gantaw 'from him'.

sentences.t: Ac yna y kymeryssant wy ganheat, ac y dechreussant gerdet a'r moch.
sentences.l: And then it-was they-took they leave, and they-began travelling with the pigs.
sentences.i: Then they took their leave and set off with the swine.
sentences.n: y kymeryssant 'they took', 3 pl. preterite (-yssant) of kymryt. ganheat ← kanheat 'leave, permission', softened as the object. y dechreussant 'they began'. gerdet ← kerdet 'go, travel', softened after the verb.

sentences.t: “A geimeit,” heb y Guydyon, “reit yw in gerdet yn bryssur.
sentences.l: “O warriors,” said Gwydion, “need is to-us travelling hastily.
sentences.i: “Warriors,” said Gwydion, “we must make haste.
sentences.n: A geimeit 'O champions': keimeit, plural of keimyat 'champion, warrior', softened after the vocative a. reit yw in 'there is need to us', we must: in 'to us', y conjugated (1 pl.). yn bryssur 'hastily'.

sentences.t: Ny phara yr hut namyn o'r pryt pwy gilyd.”
sentences.l: The magic will-not-last but from the hour till-the-other.”
sentences.i: The enchantment lasts only from one hour to the same hour next day.”
sentences.n: Ny phara 'will not last': para, with the spirant mutation after ny (p > ph). namyn 'but, except'. o'r pryt pwy gilyd 'from the time to its fellow': pryt here is 'time, hour', and pwy gilyd 'till the other', that is, a day and a night.

sentences.t: A'r nos honno y kerdyssant hyt ygwarthaf Keredigyawn, y lle a elwir etwa o achaus hynny Mochtref.
sentences.l: And that night it-was they-travelled as-far-as the-top of-Ceredigion, the place that is-called still from-cause of-that Mochdref.
sentences.i: And that night they travelled as far as the uplands of Ceredigion, to the place which for that reason is still called Mochdref.
sentences.n: y kerdyssant 'they travelled', 3 pl. preterite of kerdet. ygwarthaf 'in the top of': yn + gwarthaf with the nasal mutation; left undivided, as in the second witness. Keredigyawn: so spelled here (Kyredigyawn at the start of the part). a elwir etwa 'which is still called'. o achaus hynny 'because of that': achaus is a spelling of achaws 'cause'. Mochtref 'pig-town' (moch + tref), modern Mochdref; the first of the names along the route that recall the swine.

sentences.t: A thrannoeth y kymeryssant eu hynt; dros Elenit y doethant.
sentences.l: And next-day it-was they-took their way; over Elenydd it-was they-came.
sentences.i: And the next day they went on their way, and came over Elenydd.
sentences.n: A thrannoeth 'and the next day': trannoeth with spirant after a. eu hynt 'their way': hynt takes h after eu. dros Elenit 'over Elenydd', the high moorland of mid Wales.

sentences.t: A'r nos honno y buant y rwng Keri ac Arwystli, yn y dref a elwir heuyt o achaus hynny Mochtref.
sentences.l: And that night it-was they-were between Ceri and Arwystli, in the town that is-called also from-cause of-that Mochdref.
sentences.i: And that night they were between Ceri and Arwystli, in the township also called Mochdref for that reason.
sentences.n: y buant 'they were', 3 pl. preterite of bot; with a time phrase, 'they spent (the night)'. y rwng 'between'. Ceri and Arwystli are neighbouring districts in the uplands of Powys. y dref ← tref 'township', softened after the feminine article. heuyt 'also'.

sentences.t: Ac odyna y kerdyssant racdunt, a'r nos honno yd aethant hyt yg kymwt ym Powys, a elwir o'r ystyr hwnnw heuyt Mochnant, ac yno y buant y nos honno.
sentences.l: And from-there it-was they-travelled forward, and that night it-was they-went as-far-as to a-commote in Powys, that is-called from that reason also Mochnant, and there they-were that night.
sentences.i: And from there they travelled on, and that night they went as far as a commote in Powys which for the same reason is called Mochnant, and there they spent the night.
sentences.n: odyna 'from there'. racdunt 'forward, on', rac conjugated (3 pl.). yg kymwt 'into a commote': yn before K written yg, as yg Kaer. kymwt 'commote', a subdivision of a cantref. ym Powys 'in Powys': yn becomes ym before P, the P left plain. o'r ystyr hwnnw 'for that reason (meaning)'. Mochnant 'pig-stream' (moch + nant).

sentences.t: Ac odynha y kerdyssant hyt yg cantref Ros, ac yno y buant y nos honno y mywn y dref a elwir etwa Mochtref.
sentences.l: And from-there it-was they-travelled as-far-as to the-cantref of-Rhos, and there they-were that night in the town that is-called still Mochdref.
sentences.i: And from there they travelled to the cantref of Rhos, and there they spent the night in the township still called Mochdref.
sentences.n: odynha, the same word as odyna 'from there', spelled with nh. yg cantref 'into the cantref': yn before c written yg. Ros is Rhos, in the north-east of Gwynedd. y mywn 'in, within'. The third Mochdref of the journey.

sentences.t: “Ha wyr,” heb y Gwydyon, “ni a gyrchwn kedernit Gwynet a'r aniueileit hynn.
sentences.l: “Ho men,” said Gwydion, “we it-is-that will-make-for the-stronghold of-Gwynedd with these animals.
sentences.i: “Ho, men,” said Gwydion, “we will make for the strongholds of Gwynedd with these animals.
sentences.n: Evans prints the H of Ha as a decorated letter. Ha wyr 'ho, men': wyr ← gwyr, softened in address. Gwydyon: so spelled here, with gw. a gyrchwn 'will make for': kyrchwn, 1 pl. present of kyrchu 'go to, attack', softened after a. kedernit 'strength, stronghold', here the fastness of Gwynedd. Gwynet is Gwynedd with final -t.

sentences.t: Yd ys yn lluydaw yn an ol.”
sentences.l: One-is hosting after us.”
sentences.i: There is a muster behind us.”
sentences.n: Yd ys 'one is': the impersonal present of bot, with the particle yd. yn lluydaw 'raising a host, hosting' (llu 'host'). yn an ol 'after us': yn ol 'after' with an 'our' set inside it.

sentences.t: Sef y kyrchyssant y dref uchaf o Arllechwoed, ac yno gwneuthur creu y'r moch, ac o'r achaws hwnnw y dodet Creuwryon ar y dref.
sentences.l: That-is, they-made-for the town highest of Arllechwedd, and there making a-sty for the pigs, and from that cause it-was was-put Creuwrion on the town.
sentences.i: So they made for the highest township of Arllechwedd, and there they built a sty for the swine; and for that reason the township was given the name Creuwrion.
sentences.n: Sef y kyrchyssant 'that is, they made for': here sef leads straight to the verb with the particle y. y dref uchaf 'the highest township'. Arllechwoed is Arllechwedd, a cantref of Gwynedd. gwneuthur creu 'making a sty': creu 'pig-sty'; the verbal noun carries the narrative. y dodet 'was put', impersonal preterite of dodi. Creuwryon contains creu 'sty'; the rest of the name is not clear, and the English uses a modern spelling of the White Book's form.

sentences.t: Ac yna guedy gwneuthur creu y'r moch y kyrchyssant ar Uath uab Mathonwy, hyt yg Kaer Tathyl.
sentences.l: And then after making a-sty for the pigs it-was they-made-for Math son of Mathonwy, as-far-as to Caer Dathyl.
sentences.i: And when they had made the sty for the swine, they went to Math son of Mathonwy at Caer Dathyl.
sentences.n: guedy gwneuthur 'after making': guedy with the verbal noun. ar Uath ← Math, softened after ar. Kaer Tathyl: Evans prints a T here (col. 86), and Kaer Dathyl in cols 81 and 87; both are kept as he prints them. The place is the same.

sentences.t: A phan doethant yno, yd oedit yn dygyuori y wlat.
sentences.l: And when they-came there, one-was raising the land.
sentences.i: And when they came there, the land was being mustered.
sentences.n: A phan 'and when': pan with spirant after a. yd oedit 'one was', the impersonal imperfect of bot (ending -it). yn dygyuori y wlat 'raising the land', calling out its men to arms.

sentences.t: “Pa chwedleu yssyd yma?” heb y Gwydyon.
sentences.l: “What tidings are here?” said Gwydion.
sentences.i: “What news is there here?” said Gwydion.
sentences.n: chwedleu 'tidings, news', plural of chwedyl. yssyd 'which is', the relative form of bot, used after a question word.

sentences.t: “Dygyuor,” heb wy, “y mae Pryderi yn ych ol chwi un cantref ar ugeint.
sentences.l: “Mustering,” said they, “is Pryderi after you you, one cantref on twenty.
sentences.i: “Pryderi is mustering the one and twenty cantrefs to come after you,” they said.
sentences.n: Dygyuor 'mustering' is put first for emphasis, and y mae Pryderi 'Pryderi is' follows; its object, un cantref ar ugeint 'one and twenty cantrefs', comes at the end. yn ych ol chwi 'after you': ych 'your' inside yn ol 'after', with chwi repeating 'you'. heb wy 'said they'.

sentences.t: Ryued uu hwyret y kerdyssawchi.”
sentences.l: A-wonder was how-slowly you-travelled-you.”
sentences.i: It was a wonder how slowly you came.”
sentences.n: Ryued 'wonder', put first. uu ← bu 'was', softened. hwyret 'so late, so slow': the equative of hwyr 'late'. y kerdyssawchi: kerdyssawch, 2 pl. preterite of kerdet, with chwi 'you' written onto it.

sentences.t: “Mae yr aniueileit yd aethawch yn eu hwysc?” heb y Math.
sentences.l: “Where-are the animals that you-went in their track?” said Math.
sentences.i: “Where are the animals you went after?” said Math.
sentences.n: Mae 'where is, where are', the interrogative mae (a different word from the mae of y mae 'is'). yd aethawch 'you went', 2 pl. preterite of mynet. yn eu hwysc 'in their track', after them: gwysc 'track, wake' after eu, written hwysc with h.

sentences.t: “Maent guedy gwneuthur creu udunt yn y cantref arall issot,” heb y Guydyon.
sentences.l: “They-are after making a-sty for-them in the cantref other below,” said Gwydion.
sentences.i: “They have had a sty made for them in the next cantref below,” said Gwydion.
sentences.n: Maent guedy gwneuthur 'they are after making': bot + guedy + verbal noun gives a perfect, 'a sty has been made'. udunt 'for them', y conjugated (3 pl.). y cantref arall 'the other cantref'. issot 'below, lower down'.

sentences.t: Ar hynny, llyma y clywynt yr utkyrn a'r dygyuor yn y wlat.
sentences.l: On that, here it-was they-heard the trumpets and the muster in the land.
sentences.i: At that, they heard the trumpets and the muster in the land.
sentences.n: Ar hynny 'on that'. llyma 'see here', setting the sound before the reader. y clywynt 'they heard': clywynt, 3 pl. imperfect of clywet. utkyrn 'trumpets', plural of utkorn.

sentences.t: Ar hynny guiscaw a wnaethant wynteu, a cherdet yny uydant ym Pennard yn Aruon.
sentences.l: On that arming they-did they-for-their-part, and travelling until they-were in Pennardd in Arfon.
sentences.i: At that they armed themselves and marched until they were at Pennardd in Arfon.
sentences.n: guiscaw a wnaethant 'arming they did', they armed: verbal noun closed by a wnaethant, 3 pl. of gwneuthur; a cherdet ← kerdet carries on in the same way. guiscaw is 'dress', here 'put on armour'. yny uydant 'until they were': uydant ← bydant, softened after yny; a present-future form of bot used in narrative. ym Pennard 'in Pennardd': yn > ym before P.

sentences.t: A'r nos honno yd ymhwelwys Guydyon uab Don a Chiluathwy y urawt, hyt yg Kaer Dathyl.
sentences.l: And that night it-was returned Gwydion son of Dôn and Gilfaethwy his brother, as-far-as to Caer Dathyl.
sentences.i: And that night Gwydion son of Dôn and Gilfaethwy his brother went back to Caer Dathyl.
sentences.n: yd ymhwelwys 'returned', 3 sg. preterite in -wys of ymchwelut 'turn back'; the singular verb stands before a double subject, as Middle Welsh allows. Guydyon is spelled with u here, as Evans prints it. a Chiluathwy 'and Gilfaethwy': ch after a 'and' is the spirant mutation of c, as though the name began Kil-; elsewhere it is written with G. Kept as Evans prints it. y urawt ← brawt, softened after y 'his'.

sentences.t: Ac yguelei Uath uab Mathonwy dodi Giluathwy a Goewyn uerch Pebin y gyscu y gyt, a chymell y morynyon allan yn amharchus, a chyscu genti o'y hanuod y nos honno.
sentences.l: And in-the-bed of-Math son of Mathonwy putting Gilfaethwy and Goewin daughter of-Pebin to sleep together, and driving the maidens out disrespectfully, and sleeping with-her against-her-will that night.
sentences.i: And in the bed of Math son of Mathonwy they laid Gilfaethwy and Goewin daughter of Pebin to sleep together, and drove the maidens out with contempt; and he lay with her against her will that night.
sentences.n: Ac yguelei Uath: Evans prints yguelei, that is yg gwelei 'in the bed of', with yn 'in' assimilated and gwely 'bed' spelled with -ei (the Red Book agrees, ygwelei). Uath ← Math, softened as Evans prints it, where plain Math would be expected after a noun; the second witness's yguely Math is not the White Book. The rest is told in verbal nouns: dodi 'putting', a chymell 'and driving' (kymell, spirant after a), a chyscu 'and sleeping' (kyscu). y gyscu 'to sleep': kyscu softened after y 'to'. Goewyn: so spelled here (col. 87), Goewin earlier. amharchus 'disrespectfully' (amharch 'dishonour'). genti 'with her', gan conjugated (3 sg. fem.). o'y hanuod 'against her will': anuod takes h after 'y 'her'.

sentences.t: Pan welsant y dyd drannoeth, kyrchu a wnaethant parth a'r lle yd oed Math uab Mathonwy a'y lu.
sentences.l: When they-saw the day next-day, making-for they-did towards the place that was Math son of Mathonwy and his host.
sentences.i: When they saw the day next morning, they made their way to the place where Math son of Mathonwy was with his host.
sentences.n: welsant ← gwelsant 'they saw', 3 pl. preterite of gwelet, softened after pan. drannoeth ← trannoeth 'next day', softened as an adverb. kyrchu a wnaethant 'making for they did', they made for. parth a'r 'towards the'. yd oed 'where was'. a'y lu 'and his host': llu softened after 'y 'his'.

sentences.t: Pan doethant, yd oed y guyr hynny yn mynet y gymryt kynghor ba tu yd arhoynt Pryderi a guyr y Deheu.
sentences.l: When they-came, there-were those men going to take counsel what side they-should-wait-for Pryderi and the men of the South.
sentences.i: When they arrived, those men were on their way to take counsel where they should await Pryderi and the men of the South.
sentences.n: y gymryt ← kymryt 'take', softened after y 'to'. ba tu 'what side', in which quarter. yd arhoynt 'they should wait for': arhoynt, 3 pl. imperfect subjunctive of aros 'wait'. guyr y Deheu 'the men of the South'.

sentences.t: Ac ar y kynghor y doethant wynteu.
sentences.l: And to the counsel it-was they-came they-for-their-part.
sentences.i: And they joined the council.
sentences.n: ar y kynghor 'to the counsel': the phrase is put first and y leads to doethant 'they came'. wynteu 'they for their part', Gwydion and Gilfaethwy.

sentences.t: Sef a gaussant yn eu kynghor, aros yg kedernit Gwyned yn Aruon.
sentences.l: That-is what they-got in their counsel: waiting in the-stronghold of-Gwynedd in Arfon.
sentences.i: What they resolved in council was to wait in the fastness of Gwynedd, in Arfon.
sentences.n: Sef a gaussant 'what they got', what they decided (as at Pryderi's council earlier). aros 'waiting', the verbal noun naming the decision. yg kedernit 'in the stronghold', yn written yg before k.

sentences.t: Ac yghymherued y dwy uaynawr yd arhoed, Maynawr Bennard a Maynawr Coet Alun.
sentences.l: And in-the-middle of the two maenors it-was there-was-waiting, Maenor Bennardd and Maenor Coed Alun.
sentences.i: And they waited between the two maenors, the Maenor of Pennardd and the Maenor of Coed Alun.
sentences.n: yghymherued 'in the middle of': yn + kymherued with the nasal mutation written gh, as in yg Heredigyawn; left undivided, as in the second witness. y dwy uaynawr 'the two maenors': dwy, the feminine of 'two', softens maynawr > uaynawr. A maenor was a unit of land, a group of townships. yd arhoed 'there was waiting': arhoed is the impersonal preterite of aros. Maynawr Bennard: Pennard softened after the feminine maynawr. Coet Alun is Coed Alun.

sentences.t: A Phyderi a'y kyrchwys yno wynt; ac yno y bu y gyfranc, ac y llas lladua uawr o pop parth, ac y bu reit y wyr y Deheu enkil.
sentences.l: And Pryderi it-was-that attacked-them there they; and there was the battle, and was-slain a-slaughter great from every side, and there-was need to the men of the South to-retreat.
sentences.i: And Pryderi attacked them there; and there the battle was fought, and great slaughter was made on both sides, and the men of the South had to fall back.
sentences.n: A Phyderi: so Evans prints it, without the r; a readable slip for Phryderi (Pryderi with spirant after a 'and'), kept as written. a'y kyrchwys 'attacked them': 'y is the infixed object, pointing forward to wynt 'them'; kyrchwys is the 3 sg. preterite in -wys of kyrchu. y gyfranc ← kyfranc 'encounter, fight', softened after the feminine article. y llas 'was slain': llas is the impersonal preterite of llad. lladua uawr 'great slaughter': mawr softened after the feminine lladua. o pop parth 'from every side' (pob written pop). y wyr ← gwyr, softened after y 'to'. enkil 'retreat', a verbal noun.

sentences.t: Sef lle yd enkilyssant, hyt y lle a elwir etwa Nant Call; a hyt yno yd ymlidywyd.
sentences.l: That-is the place they-retreated, as-far-as the place that is-called still Nant Call; and as-far-as there it-was they-were-pursued.
sentences.i: They fell back as far as the place still called Nant Call; and they were pursued all the way there.
sentences.n: Sef lle yd enkilyssant 'that is the place they retreated (to)'. enkilyssant, 3 pl. preterite of enkil. hyt y lle 'as far as the place'. yd ymlidywyd 'there was pursuing', they were pursued: ymlidywyd is the impersonal preterite (ending -wyd) of ymlit 'pursue'.

sentences.t: Ac yna y bu yr ayrua diueuessur y meint.
sentences.l: And then there-was the slaughter without-measure its size.
sentences.i: And there the slaughter was beyond all measure.
sentences.n: ayrua 'slaughter, battle-carnage' (aer 'battle'). diueuessur: so Evans prints it, with -ue- written twice; the Red Book and the second witness have diuessur 'measureless' (di- 'without' + messur 'measure', softened). The dittography is kept as written. y meint 'its size', of its extent.

sentences.t: Ac yna y kilyssant hyt y lle a elwir Dol Penmaen.
sentences.l: And then it-was they-withdrew as-far-as the place that is-called Dôl Benmaen.
sentences.i: And then they fell back to the place called Dôl Benmaen.
sentences.n: y kilyssant 'they withdrew', 3 pl. preterite of kilyaw 'retreat' (the same root as enkil). Dol Penmaen: Evans prints pen maen as two words; divided as in the second witness. The modern place is Dolbenmaen, and the English uses that form.

sentences.t: Ac yna clymu a wnaethant, a cheissaw ymdangneuedu, a gwystlaw a wnaeth Pryderi ar y tangneued.
sentences.l: And then drawing-together they-did, and seeking to-make-peace-with-one-another, and giving-hostages did Pryderi on the peace.
sentences.i: And there they came to terms and sought to make peace, and Pryderi gave hostages for the peace.
sentences.n: clymu a wnaethant 'binding they did': clymu is 'tie, knot, bind'; here probably 'they came together, came to terms', but the exact sense is uncertain. a cheissaw ← keissaw 'seek', spirant after a. ymdangneuedu 'make peace with one another': the reciprocal prefix ym- + tangneuedu (tangneued 'peace'), softened. gwystlaw a wnaeth 'giving hostages did (Pryderi)'. ar y tangneued 'on the peace', as surety for it.

sentences.t: Sef a wystlwys, Gwrgi Guastra, ar y pedwyryd ar ugeint o ueibyon guyrda.
sentences.l: That-is whom he-pledged: Gwrgi Gwastra, as the fourth on twenty of sons of-noblemen.
sentences.i: As hostage he gave Gwrgi Gwastra and twenty-three others, sons of noblemen.
sentences.n: Sef a wystlwys 'what (whom) he gave as hostage': wystlwys ← gwystlwys, 3 sg. preterite of gwystlaw, softened after a. ar y pedwyryd ar ugeint 'on the fourth on twenty': the same idiom as ar uyn deudecuet, so Gwrgi Gwastra was one of twenty-four. pedwyryd 'fourth' (modern pedwerydd), as Evans prints it. guyrda 'noblemen' (gwyr + da).

sentences.t: A guedy hynny, kerdet o honunt yn eu tangneued hyt y Traeth Mawr;
sentences.l: And after that, travelling by-them in their peace as-far-as the Traeth Mawr;
sentences.i: After that they travelled under their truce as far as Traeth Mawr;
sentences.n: kerdet o honunt 'travelling by them', they travelled: the verbal noun with its subject given by o (o honunt, o conjugated, 3 pl.). yn eu tangneued 'in their peace', under the truce. Traeth Mawr 'the Great Strand', the estuary of the Glaslyn. The sentence runs on in the next unit.

sentences.t: ac ual y gyt ac y doethant hyt y Uelen Ryd y pedyt ny ellit eu reoli o ymsaethu, gyrru kennadeu o Pryderi y erchi guahard y deulu, ac erchi gadu y ryngtaw ef a Guydyon uab Don, canys ef a baryssei hynny.
sentences.l: and as soon as they-came as-far-as the Felenrhyd, the foot-soldiers could-not-be ruled from shooting-at-one-another, sending messengers by Pryderi to ask restraining the two-hosts, and asking leaving it between-him and Gwydion son of Dôn, since he it-was-that had-caused that.
sentences.i: and as soon as they reached Y Felenrhyd, the foot-soldiers could not be kept from shooting at one another; so Pryderi sent messengers asking that the two hosts be held back, and that the matter be left between himself and Gwydion son of Dôn, since it was he who had caused it.
sentences.n: ual y gyt ac y doethant 'as soon as they came'. y Uelen Ryd ← Melen Ryd 'the yellow ford', softened after the feminine article: Y Felenrhyd. y pedyt 'the foot-soldiers'. ny ellit 'one could not': ellit ← gellit, impersonal imperfect of gallu. reoli 'rule, control'. o ymsaethu 'from shooting at one another' (ym- reciprocal). gyrru kennadeu o Pryderi 'sending messengers by Pryderi': the verbal noun with its doer given by o. guahard 'forbid, restrain'. y deulu may be read two ways: y 'the' + deulu ← deu lu 'two hosts' (compare y deu lu just after), or y 'his' + teulu 'warband', softened; the first is followed here. gadu y ryngtaw ef 'leave it between him', rwng conjugated (3 sg. masc.). canys 'since'. a baryssei 'had caused', the pluperfect (-yssei) of peri.

sentences.t: At Math uab Mathonwy y doeth y genhat.
sentences.l: To Math son of Mathonwy it-was came the message.
sentences.i: The message came to Math son of Mathonwy.
sentences.n: The phrase is put first and y leads to doeth 'came'. y genhat ← kenhat 'message, embassy', softened after the feminine article.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb y Math, “e rof a Duw, os da gan Wydyon uab Don, mi a'e gadaf yn llawen.
sentences.l: “Yes,” said Math, “between me and God, if good with Gwydion son of Dôn, I it-is-that will-allow-it gladly.
sentences.i: “Yes,” said Math, “between me and God, if Gwydion son of Dôn is content, I will allow it gladly.
sentences.n: heb y Math 'said Math' (heb y before a name). e rof a Duw 'between me and God', the oath, with e for y as Evans prints it (y rof a Duw elsewhere). os da gan Wydyon 'if (it is) good with Gwydion': Gwydyon softened after gan. a'e gadaf 'I will allow it': 'e is a spelling of the infixed object 'y 'it'; gadaf, 1 sg. present-future of gadu 'leave, allow'.

sentences.t: Ni chymellaf inheu ar neb uynet e ymlad, dros wneuthur ohanam ninheu an gallu.”
sentences.l: I-will-not-compel I-for-my-part on anyone to-go to fight, instead-of doing by-us we-for-our-part our power.”
sentences.i: I will not compel anyone to go to battle in our place, when we ourselves might be doing our utmost.”
sentences.n: Ni chymellaf 'I will not compel': kymellaf with spirant after ni; cymell ar 'compel (someone)'. uynet ← mynet 'go', softened as the verbal noun after ar neb. e ymlad 'to fight': e for y 'to', as Evans prints it. dros wneuthur ohanam ninheu an gallu 'instead of our doing our utmost': dros 'for, instead of', which softens gwneuthur > wneuthur; ohanam 'by us', o conjugated (1 pl.), giving the doer; an gallu 'our power'. The sense of dros here ('instead of' or 'beyond') is not certain.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb y kennadeu, “teg, med Pryderi, oed y'r gwr a wnaeth hynn idaw ef o gam, dodi y gorf yn erbyn y eidaw ynteu, a gadu y deu lu yn segur.”
sentences.l: “Assuredly,” said the messengers, “fair, says Pryderi, would-be to the man that did this to-him he of wrong, putting his body against his-own he-for-his-part, and leaving the two hosts idle.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” said the messengers, “it would be fair, says Pryderi, for the man who did him this wrong to set his own body against his, and leave the two hosts idle.”
sentences.n: Dioer 'assuredly' (house: 'indeed' in the English). teg … oed 'fair would be', with oed as conditional. med Pryderi 'says Pryderi': med 'says', used only to report another's words. y'r gwr 'for the man'. o gam 'of wrong': kam softened after o; a wnaeth hynn idaw ef o gam 'who did him this as a wrong'. y gorf ← korf 'body', softened after y 'his'. y eidaw ynteu 'his own (body)', that is Pryderi's: eidaw is the possessive 'his'. segur 'idle'.

sentences.t: “Dygaf y Duw uyg kyffes, nat archaf i y wyr Gwyned ymlad drossof i, a minheu uy hun yn cael ymlad a Phryderi.
sentences.l: “I-take to God my confession, that I-will-not-ask I to the men of-Gwynedd fighting for-me I, and I-for-my-part my self able to-fight with Pryderi.
sentences.i: “I take God to witness that I will not ask the men of Gwynedd to fight for me, when I myself may fight with Pryderi.
sentences.n: No tag: Gwydion speaks (the second witness supplies heb y Guydyon; the White Book does not have it and the context makes it plain). Dygaf y Duw uyg kyffes 'I bring my confession to God', an oath. uyg kyffes 'my confession': uy 'my' causes the nasal mutation, written here as g on the possessive with the k left plain. nat archaf 'that I will not ask', 1 sg. present-future of erchi. y wyr Gwyned 'to the men of Gwynedd': gwyr softened after y 'to'. drossof 'for me', dros conjugated (1 sg.). a minheu uy hun yn cael ymlad 'and I myself getting to fight': an absolute clause, 'when I can fight'. a Phryderi 'with Pryderi', spirant after a.

sentences.t: Mi a dodaf uyg korf yn erbyn y eidaw yn llawen.”
sentences.l: I it-is-that will-put my body against his-own gladly.”
sentences.i: I will set my body against his gladly.”
sentences.n: Mi a dodaf 'I will put', 1 sg. present-future of dodi. uyg korf 'my body', the nasal mutation written on uy again. y eidaw 'his', as in the messengers' words, which Gwydion turns back.

sentences.t: A hynny a anuonet at Pryderi.
sentences.l: And that it-was-that was-sent to Pryderi.
sentences.i: And that answer was sent to Pryderi.
sentences.n: A hynny a anuonet 'and that was sent': the subject first, then a and the impersonal preterite anuonet of anuon 'send'.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb y Pryderi, “nit archaf inheu y neb gouyn uy iawn namyn my hun.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said Pryderi, “I-will-not-ask I-for-my-part to anyone demanding my right but my self.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” said Pryderi, “I too will ask no one to seek my redress but myself.”
sentences.n: nit archaf inheu 'I for my part will not ask'. y neb 'to anyone'. gouyn 'demand, seek' (modern gofyn). uy iawn 'my right, my due', redress for the wrong done. my hun 'myself', with my for uy.

sentences.t: E gwyr hynny a neilltuwyt, ac a dechreuwyt gwiscaw amdanunt, ac ymlad a wnaethant.
sentences.l: The men those were-set-apart, and was-begun arming them, and fighting they-did.
sentences.i: The two men were set apart, and they began to arm them, and they fought.
sentences.n: E gwyr hynny 'those men': E is the article y, so printed by Evans. a neilltuwyt 'were set apart': neilltuwyt, impersonal preterite (-wyt) of neilltuaw 'set aside'. a dechreuwyt 'was begun', impersonal preterite of dechreu. gwiscaw amdanunt 'dressing about them', putting their armour on them. ymlad a wnaethant 'fighting they did', they fought.

sentences.t: Ac o nerth grym ac angerd, a hut a lledrith, Guydyon a oruu, a Phryderi a las, ac y Maen Tyuyawc, uch y Uelen Ryd y cladwyt, ac yno y may y ued.
sentences.l: And from strength of-might and fury, and magic and illusion, Gwydion it-was-that won, and Pryderi it-was-that was-slain; and at Maen Tyfiawg above the Felenrhyd it-was he-was-buried, and there is his grave.
sentences.i: And by strength and force and fury, and by magic and enchantment, Gwydion prevailed, and Pryderi was slain; and at Maen Tyfiawg, above Y Felenrhyd, he was buried, and there his grave is.
sentences.n: o nerth grym ac angerd 'from strength, might and fury': nerth and grym are both 'strength, force'; angerd 'fury, ardour'. hut a lledrith 'magic and illusion', the two words for Gwydion's craft. a oruu 'won': oruu ← goruu, preterite of goruot 'overcome'. a las 'was slain': las ← llas, softened after a. y Maen Tyuyawc: y here stands for yn 'at' (or y 'to'), with nothing written for the mutation; Maen Tyfiawg is a stone above Y Felenrhyd. uch 'above'. y cladwyt 'he was buried', impersonal preterite of cladu. y may y ued 'there is his grave': may is mae, and ued ← bed 'grave', softened after y 'his'.

sentences.t: Gwyr y Deheu a gerdassant ac argan truan ganthunt parth ac eu gwlat, ac nit oed ryued; eu harglwyd a gollyssynt, a llawer oc eu goreuguyr, ac eu meirch, ac eu harueu can mwyaf.
sentences.l: The men of the South it-was-that travelled with lament pitiful with-them towards their land, and it-was-not a-wonder: their lord they-had-lost, and many of their best-men, and their horses, and their arms for the most.
sentences.i: The men of the South went back towards their own land lamenting bitterly, and no wonder: they had lost their lord, and many of their best men, and their horses, and most of their arms.
sentences.n: Gwyr y Deheu a gerdassant 'the men of the South went': gerdassant ← kerdassant, 3 pl. preterite of kerdet, softened after a. argan 'lament, keening'; truan 'pitiful, wretched'. ganthunt 'with them', gan conjugated (3 pl.). parth ac 'towards'. nit oed ryued 'it was no wonder'. eu harglwyd 'their lord': h before the vowel after eu. a gollyssynt 'they had lost': the pluperfect (-yssynt) of colli. oc eu 'of their'. goreuguyr 'best men'. eu harueu 'their arms' (Evans has harueu). can mwyaf 'for the most part'. The part ends here, in col. 89.
